display_name: NATO-side emitters, receivers and jammers of the 1980s, and each side's threat library
status: E1 data set (October 2026). Band and year facts come from public encyclopaedic pages (tier 4: for NATO equipment these are the operator-country reference tier available online); everything numeric that no source gives (power, gain, sensitivity, bearing accuracy, PRF windows) is a labelled estimate of the system CLASS from the textbooks in docs/SOURCES.md, not a measurement of a particular set. Sources that were not reachable (US Army FM 100-2-3, Soviet and NATO threat handbooks) are listed in docs/research/EM_E1_NATO_DATA_2026-10.md with what to read for.
notes: Used with data/em/osa_ak.json: the red ESM library 'red_esm_nato_view' is what the Warsaw Pact side believed about NATO emitters; the blue RWR library 'blue_rwr_nato_view' is what NATO believed about Soviet ones (including the SA-8). Both are beliefs, deliberately wider than the truth.

threat_libraries.name: What NATO RWRs believed about Soviet emitters (US Army FM 100-2-3, 1991)
threat_libraries.notes: From the US Army's own handbook of Soviet equipment: radar names, the old NATO/ECM letter bands and the ranges FM 100-2-3 gives (p. 5-138). The manual gives letters, not GHz; they are read here with the contemporary scheme (C 0.5-1, E 2-3, G 4-6, H 6-8, I 8-10, J 10-20 GHz; A below 0.25), which is the reader's conversion, not the manual's, so every window is low confidence. It is what NATO believed in 1991, not proof of what the Soviet radars did (the manual says 'probably' for the SA-8's bands): wider than the truth on purpose. PRF and pulse width are not given: not constrained. Do not treat these figures as gospel.

arms.name: AGM-45 Shrike class anti-radiation missile (broad E-I band head)

freq_min_hz.source: arm_refs (designation-systems.net AGM-45: the A-10/B-10 head, broad E- to I-band)
freq_min_hz.notes: The other heads are narrower (E/F, G, I alone): none of them covers the J band of the Osa's tracking radar. E 2-3, I 8-10 GHz on the contemporary letter scheme (EM_E1_NATO_DATA).

tune_fraction.source: arm_refs (the seeker tuned to a fixed frequency range: the head's whole band)

prf_fraction.source: estimate: a crystal-video head with angle gating, no signal sorting

sensitivity_dbw.source: estimate (ew_textbooks: crystal video with preamplification, -50 dBm)
sensitivity_dbw.notes: Enough to hear a search radar's sidelobes at tens of km, so a turning antenna is followed continuously, not only once a turn.

fov_deg.source: estimate; arm_refs (the seeker not gimballed, a fixed, limited field of view: the missile had to be nearly aligned with the emitter)

angle_sigma_deg.source: estimate (ew_textbooks: amplitude-comparison seeker, about a degree)

resolution_deg.source: estimate: two emitters closer than about three beamwidths of its error are one direction

speed_mps.source: arm_refs (Mach 2); estimate (the average over a low-level flight, below the top speed)

loft_deg.source: arm_refs (fired lofted toward a suspected site; the seeker took over on the way down); the angle an estimate

lethal_radius_m.source: estimate: arm_refs' 66.6-67.5 kg blast-fragmentation warhead against a radar's antennas and cabin

rcs_m2.source: estimate: a 3 m, 20 cm missile nose-on

arms.notes: No memory: 'if the SAM radar switched off, missiles already fired lost lock and went ballistic' (arm_refs). In service 1965-1992 (US).

arms.name: AGM-88A HARM class anti-radiation missile

freq_min_hz.source: estimate: the band of the launch aircraft's warning receiver (nato_ew_refs, ALR-46 2-18 GHz); arm_refs gives no band for the WGU-2/B head

freq_max_hz.source: estimate (as freq_min_hz); covers the J band

tune_fraction.source: estimate; arm_refs (the seeker pre-tuned to the likely threats; the launch computer selects the target)
tune_fraction.notes: It homes on the signal the launch computer gave it: a decoy on the radar's own parameters is the same signal to it.

sensitivity_dbw.source: estimate (ew_textbooks: a superheterodyne-class seeker, more sensitive than a crystal video head)

fov_deg.source: estimate (a body-fixed broadband seeker with a wide field)

speed_mps.source: arm_refs (Mach 2+); estimate (the average at low level)

max_flight_s.source: derived: 48 km (usaf_harm_factsheet, '30 plus miles') at 700 m/s, with margin

loft_deg.source: arm_refs (pre-briefed: a lofted launch toward a known threat); the angle an estimate
loft_deg.notes: Raised from 10 deg while testing the ARM drill (20 Oct 2026): at 10 deg the missile topped out near 850 m from a 300 m launch at 22 km and came in on a 2-3 deg glide, so a remembered point 400 m long still passed within the lethal radius of the radar. A lofted, pre-briefed HARM comes down steeply; 20 deg is still an estimate.

lethal_radius_m.source: estimate: arm_refs' WDU-21/B, 66 kg blast-fragmentation with about 25,000 steel fragments, laser proximity fuze FMU-111/B

rcs_m2.source: estimate: a 4.2 m, 25 cm missile nose-on

max_range_m.source: arm_refs (Wikipedia AGM-88: 25 km in a low-level launch; usaf_harm_factsheet 48 km and more from altitude)
max_range_m.notes: The raids against the battery fly low; a launch from altitude reaches further (set the carrier's own range in the scenario).

arms.notes: Memory: 'an internal inertial system keeps the missile heading toward the target after it has locked on once, though CEP is larger' (arm_refs, designation-systems.net). First delivered 1983; US Navy IOC 1985, USAF 1987; first used April 1986.
